intended_object: The rigid motion of the Euclidean plane q ↦ R q + p: apply the linear isometry R, then translate by p. Inferred from the docstring and the surrounding moving-sofa module, which compares the two composition conventions.
explanation: The body R.toAffineIsometryEquiv.trans (AffineIsometryEquiv.vaddConst ℝ p) applies R first and then v ↦ v +ᵥ p = v + p. The composite therefore sends q to R q + p, which the library checks with rotateThenTranslate_apply, proved by rfl. This matches the docstring exactly, and the result is an affine isometric equivalence of the plane, as intended. The formula would make sense in any normed space, but this is a convention helper inside a formalization fixed to Plane = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2). The plane is required by the problem and its pinned upstream formalization, including the orientation instance and rotation by an angle, so the definition is not a general notion re-implemented in a special case. Mathlib has no single declaration for this composite; it is built directly from two Mathlib constructions, LinearIsometryEquiv.toAffineIsometryEquiv and AffineIsometryEquiv.vaddConst.
